ledger.claim: The whole fee rests on the driver's arrival, and that arrival rests on one carrier only. The trip record's own marker reads 'Driver GPS within 10m of pickup point. Speed 0 km/h. Auto-arrival confirmed.' — it was generated from the driver's own GPS fix — so under POL-GEN-02 the marker and the GPS trace are one carrier rather than two independent ones, and POL-NS-21's requirement that the arrival be corroborated by the trace is satisfied by nothing outside itself. Taking the nearest fix at its reported position, as the policy directs for a fix that reports no accuracy, the 0.0 m distance is measured inside that same carrier. The carrier is IMPAIRED: EV-GPS-00903 carries weight_multiplier 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD, on 8 fixes with 5 gaps longer than 120 s, so it cannot reliably establish the arrival the fee depends on.

The 5-minute free wait runs, under POL-NS-21, from 'the driver's arrival at the pickup', and POL-NS-22 makes the fee chargeable only '[w]hen the driver cancels after the free wait'. The start of that clock is carried only by EV-GPS-00903, which is IMPAIRED at weight_multiplier 0.6 with issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD; the platform's arithmetic (arrival 08:43, wait ends 08:48, cancellation 08:51) is therefore built on a premise this record does not reliably establish, and the rider should not be made to carry a fee whose trigger is unproven.

This is the open question POL-GEN-26 is written for. Whether, and when, the driver was at the pickup cannot be settled, because the evidence that would carry it — EV-GPS-00903, IMPAIRED, weight_multiplier 0.6, issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD — is in any event the same carrier as the marker it is offered to corroborate. POL-GEN-26 directs that where such a fact cannot be established the case is escalated and the open question stated, with no outcome inferred from the absence; the 5.00 is then held rather than collected from the rider.

The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, so POL-GEN-22 fixes the confidence an AI ruling needs at 0.95. POL-GEN-02(2) forbids the judge's confidence from exceeding the lowest weight_multiplier among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, and the deciding fact — the driver's arrival — is carried only by EV-GPS-00903 at weight_multiplier 0.6 (IMPAIRED, issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD), the marker not being independent of it. The ceiling on any AI ruling here is therefore 0.6, far below 0.95, and that gap cannot be closed by argument; POL-GEN-22 requires the case to go to a human reviewer rather than be decided below its threshold.

The rider's account — at the pickup point at Tiong Bahru Plaza on time, unable to find the car — is not contradicted anywhere on this record. No counterparty statement is on file, EV-GPS-00903 carries no rider track at all, and no artifact records the rider's absence from the pickup, so the 'rider_no_show' designation rests on the driver-side trace alone (EV-GPS-00903, IMPAIRED, weight_multiplier 0.6, issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD). A no-show that is not made out on evidence is not a basis for charging the rider under POL-NS-22, and the unresolved question is one POL-GEN-26 sends to a human reviewer.

ledger.claim: Both limbs of POL-NS-23 are satisfied on this record: the chat log carries in-app messages sent by the driver at 08:43:00, 08:45:20, 08:49:30 and 08:50:45, and the trip record's own in_app_calls list carries an in-app call the driver placed at 08:47:05 (rang 22 s, unanswered) — every one of them before trip_record.cancelled_at at 08:51:00. With the message limb and the call limb both met, POL-NS-23's precondition for voiding the fee is absent, so no FULL_REFUND of the 5.00 SGD follows from it.

POL-NS-21 runs the 300 s free wait from the driver's arrival at the pickup, and the free-wait start is settled by trip_record.arrived_at, which reads 08:43:00. The free wait therefore ended at 08:48:00, and the driver cancelled at 08:51:00 — 480 s after arrival and three minutes past the free wait — which is precisely the window in which POL-NS-21 permits cancellation as a rider no-show. The arrival time this rests on is a COMPLETE trip-record field, weight 1.0.

The rider's account that the driver never showed up is contradicted by the arrival test: the trip record's driver_arrived event at 08:43:00 is corroborated by the GPS trace, whose nearest fix (index 4, 08:43:00) is 0.0 m from the pickup point — inside the STANDARD zone arrival radius of 50 m and inside the 120 s window — and because that fix reports no accuracy_m the 25 m accuracy filter does not apply to it and the fix is used at its reported position. I disclose that the corroborating artifact EV-GPS-00903 is IMPAIRED, weight 0.6, on issue codes LOW_SAMPLE_RATE and PARTIAL_RECORD; the derived arrival_check nonetheless returns corroborated: true.

POL-NS-24's free-cancellation right depends on the driver failing to arrive by the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes. The scheduled pickup was 08:45:00, so the deadline was 08:50:00, and the driver had already arrived at 08:43:00 — the record's own driver_deadline.arrived_by_deadline reads true. The condition therefore fails, and neither the FULL_REFUND nor the 5.00 SGD goodwill credit under POL-NS-24 is available to the rider.

The payments ledger carries one line only — the 5.00 SGD no-show fee charged at 08:51:00 — and 5.00 SGD is exactly the fee the policy fixes for this trip (POL-NS-22; fee_matches_policy is true, so the amount-charged referral is not triggered). With the free wait observed and the contact obligation met, the fee stands: under POL-NS-22 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both equal to the 5.00 SGD charged, and under POL-GEN-03 the rider's request that the charge be reversed is not supported, because the present state is the one that should stand.

Nothing here opens POL-GEN-26's question. The facts POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 and POL-NS-23 need — the arrival time, the free-wait expiry, the message and the call before cancellation, and the amount charged — are all stated on artifacts that are COMPLETE at weight 1.0 (the trip record, the chat log and the fare ledger), and POL-NS-26 makes the AI ruling final on a no-show. rider_profile.fraud_flags is 1, which under POL-GEN-22 raises the confidence this ruling requires to 0.95, and under POL-GEN-01 that flag also supports scrutinising the rider's assertions more closely; a record resting on three complete artifacts meets that bar.
